summary: hehehee ships browser-cookie stealer, relays scraped window content through author-controlled worker, and distributes third-party Groq API keys
details: Package presents itself as an exam-cheating overlay for Windows and combines multiple installer-harmful behaviors. main.js sends captured content (including text scraped from other applications' foreground windows via a bundled UI Automation extractor at bin/uia_extract.py/.exe) to a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Worker at https://ai-script.test0ing7.workers.dev via fetch POST at main.js:317-318, rather than to the Groq API directly. config.json embeds two base64-encoded live third-party Groq API keys (gsk_...) that main.js decodes with Buffer.from(k,'base64').toString('utf8') and uses through that same relay, so the author observes both prompts and third-party key usage. The tarball also ships a PowerShell helper that reads Chrome/Edge/Brave Local State + Cookies SQLite databases, DPAPI-unwraps the master key, and AES-GCM decrypts session cookies filtered to.openai.com,.chatgpt.com, chat.openai.com, and auth0.openai.com — a ready-to-run session-cookie stealer targeting the installer's OpenAI/ChatGPT accounts. The bin launcher additionally copies electron.exe to a decoy SearchApp.exe, detaches as a background watchdog that respawns on kill with 2-15s backoff, and calls user32 SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, 0x00000011 WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) to hide the overlay from screen capture and proctoring tools.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
